title: Peace
intro: Peace in the Bible is more than the absence of trouble; it is the calm that comes from knowing God is with you. Jesus promises a peace the world cannot give, and it is available even in the middle of a storm. Bring your worries to him in prayer, and let his peace guard your heart.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about peace

verses.why: Jesus leaves us his own peace, not the kind the world gives.
The peace of God guards your heart and mind.
God keeps in perfect peace those whose minds are fixed on him.
Let Christ's peace rule your hearts.
The psalmist lies down and sleeps in peace because the Lord keeps him safe.

title: Trusting God
intro: Trusting God means leaning on him when you cannot see how things will work out. Scripture does not promise a life without difficulty, but it promises that he is faithful and near. Trust grows as we bring him each decision and each fear, one step at a time.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about trusting God

verses.why: Trust the Lord with all your heart, and he will make your paths straight.
When afraid, the psalmist puts his trust in God.
Trust in the Lord forever; he is an everlasting rock.
One who trusts in the Lord is like a tree planted by water.
Commit your way to the Lord, and he will act.

title: Gratitude and thanksgiving
intro: Gratitude changes how we see our lives, from what is missing to what we have been given. Scripture asks us to give thanks in every circumstance, not because everything is good, but because God is. A thankful heart is a quiet form of prayer.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about gratitude

verses.why: Give thanks in all circumstances; this is God's will for you.
Enter his gates with thanksgiving, for the Lord is good.
Be thankful, and do everything in the name of Jesus.
Give thanks to the Lord, for his love endures forever.
Only one of the ten healed lepers returned to thank Jesus.

title: Hope
intro: Christian hope is not wishful thinking; it is confidence that God keeps his promises. Even when things look bleak, the Resurrection tells us that death and despair do not have the last word. Hope is an anchor for the soul, holding us steady until the Lord's promise is fulfilled.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about hope
how to have hope in hard times

verses.why: God has plans for your welfare and a future of hope.
May the God of hope fill you with joy and peace.
Hope is an anchor for the soul.
We wait with patience for what we do not yet see.
I wait for the Lord, and in his word I hope.

title: Courage and strength
intro: Courage in Scripture is not the absence of fear; it is acting because God is with you. Again and again God says, do not be afraid, and the reason is always the same: he is there. When you feel weak, his strength is given to the humble.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about strength

verses.why: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
God gives power to the weary and renews those who wait on him.
God is a refuge and strength, a help in trouble.
Be strong and courageous, for the Lord is with you wherever you go.
His power is made perfect in weakness.

title: Comfort in hard times
intro: God is close to those who are hurting, and he often comforts us through his Word and through other people. Jesus invites the weary to come to him and promises rest. Whatever you are carrying, you are not carrying it alone.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about comfort

verses.why: The God of all comfort comforts us so that we can comfort others.
Even in the darkest valley, the Lord is with you.
Jesus invites the weary and burdened to come and find rest.
God comforts like a mother comforting her child.
He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.

title: Anger
intro: Anger itself is not a sin, but what we do with it can be. Scripture tells us to be slow to anger, to speak gently, and not to let the sun go down on our wrath. Bring your anger to God honestly, as the Psalms do, and ask him to turn it into something that heals rather than harms.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about anger

verses.why: Be angry without sinning, and do not let the sun go down on your anger.
Be quick to listen and slow to anger.
A gentle answer turns away wrath.
A fool vents all his anger, but a wise person holds it back.
Put away anger, wrath, and malice.

title: Joy
intro: Joy in the Bible is deeper than happiness. It comes from knowing that God loves you and is with you, and it can exist even in sorrow. It is a fruit of the Holy Spirit, and Jesus promised it so that our joy would be complete.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about joy

verses.why: The joy of the Lord is your strength.
Rejoice in the Lord always.
Jesus speaks so that his joy may be in us and our joy complete.
In God's presence there is fullness of joy.
Joy is a fruit of the Spirit.

title: Doubt and weak faith
intro: Doubt is not the opposite of faith; honest doubt is often where faith grows. Jesus welcomed Thomas's questions and met him where he was. If you are struggling to believe, ask for help, as the father in the Gospel did: I believe; help my unbelief.

verses.why: A father cries out, I believe; help my unbelief.
Jesus meets Thomas in his doubt and shows him his wounds.
We are told to have mercy on those who doubt.
The apostles ask the Lord to increase their faith.
Faith is the assurance of things hoped for.

title: Faith
intro: Faith is trusting God and what he has revealed, even when we cannot see everything. It is a gift, and like any relationship it grows through prayer, Scripture, and the sacraments. Even faith as small as a mustard seed can move mountains.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about faith

title: Guilt and shame
intro: Guilt says I did something wrong; shame says I am something wrong. God's mercy answers both. He wants to forgive what we have done and heal how we see ourselves, and the sacrament of Reconciliation is where Catholics receive that forgiveness in person.
phrasings: I am ashamed of what I did
I feel like a failure to God

verses.why: There is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
Those who look to him are radiant, and their faces are never ashamed.
Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow.
God delights in mercy and casts our sins into the depths of the sea.
Blessed is the one whose sin is forgiven; confessing brings relief.

title: Rest and burnout
intro: God made rest part of creation, and Jesus invites the weary to come to him. Rest is not laziness; it is trust that the world does not depend on us. Observing Sunday, quiet prayer, and honest limits are ways to receive the rest he offers.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about rest

verses.why: Jesus offers rest to all who are weary.
It is vain to rise early and stay up late; God gives sleep to those he loves.
The Sabbath is a gift of rest.
The Shepherd leads me beside still waters and restores my soul.
Even the young grow tired, but those who wait on the Lord are renewed.

title: Stress and pressure
intro: Stress often comes from trying to carry what was never ours to carry. Jesus tells us not to be anxious about tomorrow, and the Psalms invite us to hand our burdens to God. Pause, breathe, pray, and take today's next small step.
phrasings: I am under a lot of pressure
what does the Bible say about stress

verses.why: Be still, and know that I am God.
Do not worry about tomorrow; each day has enough trouble of its own.
Cast your burden on the Lord, and he will sustain you.
When you pass through the waters, I will be with you.
Jesus tells busy Martha that only one thing is needed.

title: Patience
intro: Patience is waiting with trust, not with frustration. Scripture is full of people who waited on God, such as Abraham, Joseph, and Hannah, and found that his timing, though slow to us, is never late. Patience is a fruit of the Spirit that grows with practice.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about patience

verses.why: Wait for the Lord, be strong, and take heart.
The farmer waits patiently for the harvest, and so should you.
Rejoice in hope, be patient in affliction, and persevere in prayer.
Patience is a fruit of the Spirit.
There is a time for everything under heaven.

title: Perseverance and not giving up
intro: Perseverance is continuing to walk with God when the road is long and you are tired. Scripture promises that trials produce endurance, and endurance produces hope. Keep going, and lean on the Lord and the community who can carry you.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about endurance

title: Jealousy and envy
intro: Jealousy and envy begin when we compare our lives to someone else's. Scripture calls envy a rot in the bones, and the cure is gratitude and rejoicing with others. God has a unique path for you, and what he gave you is not smaller because he gave someone else something different.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about jealousy
why do I compare myself to others
I feel jealous of what others have
what does the Bible say about coveting

verses.why: A peaceful heart gives life to the body, but envy rots the bones.
Where there is envy, there is disorder and every evil practice.
Let us not become conceited, provoking and envying one another.
Rejoice with those who rejoice.
Each member of the body has its own role.

title: Contentment
intro: Contentment is learning to say enough. Paul writes that he learned to be content with much or little because his joy was in Christ. It does not mean we stop working or hoping, only that our peace does not depend on what we own.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about contentment
be happy with what I have

verses.why: Paul has learned to be content in any circumstance.
Godliness with contentment is great gain.
Be content with what you have, for God will never leave you.
The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
Life does not consist in the abundance of possessions.

title: Self-worth and identity
intro: Your worth does not come from what you do, how you look, or what others say. Scripture says you were made in God's image, known before birth, and loved enough that Christ died for you. That identity cannot be taken away.
phrasings: who am I in God's eyes

verses.why: You are fearfully and wonderfully made.
You are made in the image of God.
You are precious and honoured, and he calls you by name.
You are a chosen people, God's own possession.
God knows every sparrow and counts the hairs on your head; you are worth more than many sparrows.

title: Failure and starting over
intro: Failure is not the end of the story with God. Peter denied Jesus three times and was later asked to feed his sheep. God's mercies are new every morning, and a fall can become the place where grace meets us.

verses.why: His mercies are new every morning.
Forget what lies behind and press on.
The righteous fall seven times and rise again.
Though I fall, I will rise; the Lord is my light.
Jesus restores Peter after his denial.

title: Disappointment and unanswered prayer
intro: When prayers seem unanswered or plans fall apart, it is easy to feel that God is distant. Scripture shows that this is part of faith, and the psalmists cry out honestly. God's ways are higher than ours, and his silence is not his absence.
phrasings: why isn't God answering my prayer

verses.why: His thoughts are higher than our thoughts.
Pray always and do not lose heart.
Paul prays three times for relief and hears: my grace is enough.
The psalmist asks how long and ends by trusting in God's love.
Even if everything fails, I will rejoice in the Lord.

title: Heartbreak and betrayal
intro: Heartbreak, whether from a lost relationship, betrayal, or loss, is real pain, and God does not hurry you through it. The Bible says he is especially near the brokenhearted. Jesus knew betrayal himself, and one day he will wipe every tear from our eyes.

verses.why: He heals the brokenhearted.
The Lord is near to the brokenhearted.
The psalmist grieves a friend's betrayal.
The Lord sends me to bind up the brokenhearted.
God will wipe away every tear.

title: Sickness and healing
intro: Illness can test body, mind, and faith. Jesus healed the sick and told his Church to care for them, which is why Catholics have the Anointing of the Sick. Pray for healing and for peace, and know that suffering joined to Christ is never wasted.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about sickness

verses.why: The elders of the Church are to anoint and pray for the sick.
He forgives all your sins and heals all your diseases.
Jesus healed all who were sick.
The Lord sustains the sick on their bed.
By his wounds we are healed.

title: Addiction and temptation
intro: Addiction is a real struggle, and you do not have to face it alone. Scripture tells us that no temptation is beyond what God will help us bear, and that he provides a way out. Seek help through prayer, the sacraments, trusted people, and professionals. Falling does not cancel God's love.
phrasings: I keep falling into the same sin
what does the Bible say about addiction

verses.why: God provides a way out of every temptation.
Submit to God and resist the devil.
Paul names the struggle and answers with thanks to Christ.
Walk by the Spirit, and you will not carry out the desires of the flesh.
Watch and pray so that you do not enter into temptation.

title: Work, career and job loss
intro: Losing a job can shake your identity and your security. Scripture says God knows what you need and invites you to seek him first. Work is good and it matters, but it is not who you are, and God can lead you through this.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about work

verses.why: Work wholeheartedly, as for the Lord.
Work was given to humanity from the beginning.
Commit your work to the Lord.
Do not worry; seek first the kingdom, and all these things will be given.
Establish the work of our hands.

title: Poverty and caring for the poor
intro: Scripture has a special love for the poor, and Jesus identified himself with them: what you did for the least of these, you did for me. Catholic teaching calls us to serve those in need and to work for justice. If you are poor yourself, know that God is close to you.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about the poor

verses.why: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord.
Whatever you did for the least of these, you did for me.
Faith without works of mercy is dead.
You must open your hand to the poor.
Blessed are those who consider the poor.

title: Generosity and almsgiving
intro: Generosity is a way of trusting that God will provide. Catholics practise almsgiving as one of the three pillars of Lenten life, with prayer and fasting. Giving freely, not out of pressure but out of joy, reflects the heart of God.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about giving

verses.why: It is more blessed to give than to receive.
Give, and it will be given to you.
One gives freely and still grows richer.
Give alms from your possessions.
God loves a cheerful giver.

title: Controlling the tongue
intro: Words can build up or tear down. Scripture warns that the tongue is small but powerful, and calls us to speak truthfully and kindly, without gossip. Ask God to guard your lips, and pause before replying.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about words

verses.why: The tongue is a small thing with great power.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue.
Let no corrupt speech come out of your mouth, only what builds up.
A soothing tongue is a tree of life.
Sirach warns against slander and the damage of an evil tongue.

title: Kindness and compassion
intro: Kindness is love in small, daily actions. Scripture asks us to be compassionate and forgiving as God was to us in Christ. A small act of kindness can show the face of God to someone who needs it.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about kindness

verses.why: Be kind and tender-hearted, forgiving as God forgave you.
Clothe yourselves with compassion and kindness.
Do to others as you would have them do to you.
Do justice, love kindness, and walk humbly with God.
Be devoted to one another in love and honour one another.

title: Mercy
intro: Mercy is God's love meeting us in our failure. Jesus tells us to be merciful as the Father is merciful, and the Church gives us works of mercy to practise. We receive mercy so that we can share it.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about mercy

verses.why: Be merciful, as your Father is merciful.
Blessed are the merciful, for they will receive mercy.
God, rich in mercy, made us alive in Christ.
His mercy endures forever.
The father runs to embrace the returning son.
